subject: c10-eng

weightage.label: Language through Literature: First Flight + Footprints Without Feet (Ch 4–31)

note: Official 2026-27 theory: Reading 20, Writing Skills and Grammar 20, Literature 40; internal assessment is 20. Grammar covers determiners, tenses, modals, subject–verb concord and reported speech (commands/requests, statements, questions). Writing is a formal letter (100–120 words, 5) and an analytical paragraph (100–120 words, 5). Literature includes extracts, First Flight and Footprints Without Feet short answers, and one long answer from each book. Words and Expressions-II is prescribed but is not named in the 80-mark section-wise weightage.

reference.label: Reading: main idea and evidence
reference.text: Read for the central idea, locate supporting evidence, then answer from the passage rather than adding unsupported information.

reference.label: Inference
reference.text: Use explicit evidence from the passage plus a logical conclusion; do not turn an inference into a guess.

reference.label: Formal letter structure
reference.text: Sender's address → Date → Recipient's address → Subject → Salutation → Body → Closing.

reference.label: Analytical paragraph structure
reference.text: Introduction → key features/data → relevant comparison → conclusion. Use the given chart, graph, map or cues.

reference.label: Reported command/request
reference.text: Reporting verb + object + to/not to + base verb.

reference.label: Reported statement
reference.text: Reporting clause + that + reported clause, with tense/pronoun/time-word changes where required.

reference.label: Reported question
reference.text: Reporting verb + if/whether or wh-word + statement word order; do not keep question word order.

reference.label: Grammar checklist
reference.text: Check determiner choice, tense consistency, subject–verb concord and modal + base verb before submitting.

reference.label: Literature answer frame
reference.text: Use the text's event/detail → interpretation → evidence or example → direct conclusion. For character/theme questions, stay tied to the text.

reference.label: Reading: vocabulary and analysis
reference.text: For reading questions, use context to determine vocabulary meaning and distinguish direct retrieval, inference, analysis and evaluation; support answers with the passage.

reference.label: Literature extracts
reference.text: For prose/drama and poetry extracts, identify the context, speaker/character or poetic situation, then answer the inference, interpretation, vocabulary and literary-feature questions from the extract.

reference.label: First Flight short answers
reference.text: Practise concise 40–50-word answers that directly address interpretation, analysis, inference or evaluation; use precise textual evidence rather than plot retelling.

reference.label: Footprints Without Feet short answers
reference.text: Practise concise 40–50-word answers focused on interpretation, analysis, inference and evaluation, staying tied to the supplementary text.

reference.label: Long answers
reference.text: Prepare both prescribed long-answer patterns: First Flight questions requiring creativity, imagination and extrapolation beyond/across the text, and Footprints Without Feet questions on theme/plot, inference or character sketch, in about 100–120 words.

reference.label: Words and Expressions-II
reference.text: Keep the prescribed workbook in study coverage: Units 1–4 and Units 7–11. The syllabus prescribes it even though it is not separately named in the 80-mark section-wise weightage.

reference.label: Listening and speaking assessment
reference.text: Practise the internal listening-and-speaking component through interactive turn-taking, fluency/coherence, pronunciation, vocabulary and grammar; use regular speaking/listening practice rather than written-only preparation.

mistakes: Grammar: attempt 10 of the 12 questions; use the choice to skip the two least certain answers.
Do not copy whole sentences from a reading passage when a shorter, precise answer is enough.
Formal letter: missing subject, salutation, closing or incorrect format can cost marks even when the content is relevant.
Analytical paragraph: do not list every number mechanically; identify the main trend and compare the important features.
Reported questions: change to statement word order; do not retain the original question structure.
Literature: answer the exact demand—theme, inference, character, message or evidence—rather than retelling the entire plot.
order: Build the literature base: read First Flight and Footprints Without Feet, including the prescribed poems and stories.
Practise Reading regularly: one discursive and one case-based passage, then review wrong answers.
Master Grammar in small sets: determiners → tenses → modals → subject–verb concord → reported speech.
Practise Writing repeatedly: formal letter and analytical paragraph within the 100–120 word limit.
Finish with mixed timed papers so Reading, Grammar, Writing and Literature are practised together.
